title: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game
abstract: arXiv:2611.24888v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) now perform strongly on Alan Turing's 1950 Imitation Game, so we propose a harder challenge, the Personal Imitation Game, which asks whether a machine can replicate a specific individual in conversation rather than a generic human. Testing with 30 participants, we establish a human baseline and report the identity signals interrogators rely on: stylometric features, personality traits, and biographical facts. To demonstrate the framework, we design an LLM-based system that plays the game for one of the paper's authors, drawing on an autoethnographic dataset spanning ten years of personal digital communication. In a 20-person deception study, interrogators choose our system over the author's own friends in 7 of 10 rounds, and the author over our system in 13 of 20; neither rate is distinguishable from chance at this sample size. translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）如今在艾伦·图灵1950年提出的模仿游戏（Imitation Game）中表现出色，因此我们提出了一个更难的挑战——个人模仿游戏，它探究机器能否在对话中复制一个特定的个体，而非泛泛的普通人。通过30名参与者的测试，我们建立了人类基线，并报告了审讯者所依赖的身份信号：文体特征、人格特质和传记事实。为了展示这一框架，我们设计了一个基于LLM的系统，为论文的一位作者参与该游戏，该系统利用了涵盖十年个人数字通信的自动民族志数据集。在一项20人的欺骗研究中，审讯者在10轮中有7轮选择了我们的系统而非作者自己的朋友，在20次中有13次选择了作者而非我们的系统；在此样本量下，这两个比率均无法与随机概率区分开。我们讨论了设计改进、个人AI智能体的应用及相关影响。
tldr: 该论文提出了“个人模仿游戏”这一更难的挑战，要求机器在对话中模仿特定个体而非普通人，并利用十年个人数字通信数据构建的LLM系统实验表明，审讯者无法可靠地区分该系统与真人本人。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the Personal Imitation Game, a harder challenge asking whether a machine can replicate a specific individual in conversation, and demonstrates through an LLM system built on ten years of personal digital communication data that interrogators cannot reliably distinguish the system from the real person.
